lineage: Complements the first 25 Class II decisions in draft PR #2830; together exactly 75 unmatched Class II dates.
guardrails: All classifications are curator proposals, never owner date approval or new image rights.
An approved Prayer cover or Class I Calendar hero does not authorise reproduction on a different date.
Gallery 989 title matches are nonvisual research leads; iconographic verification precedes release.
No rejected artwork revived. The owner-rejected AI Nain treatment is not the same as a physical historic painting.
No automatic Commons image admission, no image downloads, paid licences, museum contact or new app Calendar mappings.
Do not conflate the historical slate's isSunday field with civil weekdays: five recorded flags disagree with 2026 weekday dates.
Class II research dates include special vigils and Ember Masses; do not force exact Gospel matches where proper pericopes remain unresolved.

rows.editorialReason: Reuse the previously selected Tintoretto workshop Circumcision from the Octave Day. The Gospel action is relevant, but this new Holy Name date placement is not yet authorized.

rows.observance: The Holy Family: Jesus, Mary & Joseph
rows.editorialReason: Sebastiano Ricci's Holy Family with Angels offers a Baroque alternative among nine documented leads. The feast is thematic rather than one unique narrative scene.
Giuseppe Maria Crespi's Wedding at Cana is a title-matched existing gallery lead for John 2. It has not been visually verified, owner-approved for this Sunday or cleared as a photograph.
Rubens's Saint Matthias is an exact-saint title; maintain the known work without inventing release approval.
No accurate day-specific image is recorded. Resolve the actual Ember lessons and Gospel before choosing a Gospel illustration; do not substitute unrelated Temptations of Saint Anthony.

rows.liturgicalSubjectWorkingLabel: Healing at the Pool of Bethesda

recommendedWork.title: Christ Healing at the Pool of Bethesda

rows.editorialReason: Dirck van Delen's Pool of Bethesda is an existing gallery subject lead consistent with the traditional Ember Friday Gospel. Confirm the 1962 proper and photograph before binding.
This has a multi-lesson Ember proper; artwork must follow the final Gospel/ritual context. A vague Lent image should not masquerade as an exact scene.
No exact Good Shepherd painting is recorded in the 989 title registry. Keep the explicit subject gap; do not confuse Adoration of the Shepherds with Christ the Good Shepherd.
Rubens's Resurrection already has a released Regina Caeli image. It is Paschal context only, not a literal John 16:16-22 scene; owner-scoped Calendar reuse would be required.
Restout's Pentecost is a theological anticipation of John 16, not the Gospel event itself. Existing research identity only; the archived Restout reproduction has source holds.

rows.liturgicalSubjectWorkingLabel: Ask the Father in Christ's name (John 16)
rows.editorialReason: No documented literal scene or specifically approved teaching-of-apostles painting. Preserve the thematic requirement, not a false exact-Gospel claim.
Reuse-proposal only: the Hans Süss von Kulmbach Ascension is already chosen for the feast itself on 14 May; approval does not automatically extend to the vigil.
Prefer the already chosen Ascension image as contextual anticipation of Pentecost; it does not depict the appointed Farewell Discourse Gospel.
The gallery contains Lanfranco's multiplication of loaves, which is a DIFFERENT miracle. Never reuse it for Luke 5 without replacing the subject.

recommendedWork.title: Birth of St John the Baptist

rows.editorialReason: Andrea Sacchi's Birth of John is already selected for 24 June. It can be considered for anticipatory reuse on the vigil, not silently approved.
No confirmed exact sermon/reconciliation painting in the gallery. Do not use a generic altar photograph as Gospel illustration.
No directly corresponding painting is currently tied to this date; keep an explicit scene gap rather than unrelated shepherd imagery.
Jean-Baptiste de Champaigne's martyrdom is an existing previously acceptable exact-saint subject, consistent with the preferred seventeenth-century style.
Rubens's Assumption has already been selected for 15 August. The vigil can reuse it only under explicit new date scope.
Domenico Fetti's Good Samaritan is an existing institutional catalogue artwork and a direct subject for the appointed Luke 10 Gospel.
Tissot's Ten Lepers depicts the correct Gospel; its illustrative medium differs from the preferred dark Baroque art. Keep as fallback while selecting from the existing gallery.

rows.liturgicalSubjectWorkingLabel: Lilies of the field; birds of the air (Matthew 6)
rows.editorialReason: No confirmed image of the Sermon teaching on providence. Avoid treating unrelated floral still-life as a Gospel scene.

rows.editorialReason: Prefer Altomonte's Baroque Nain painting over the later Kotarbiński lead; the previous user-rejected AI Nain image is NOT reinstated by this real-painting research proposal.

rows.observance: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.editorialReason: Louis/Mathieu Le Nain is a period-appropriate existing research attribution. Verify exact painting and attribution; do not imply the two brothers co-painted without source authority.

rows.liturgicalSubjectWorkingLabel: Healing of the man with dropsy

recommendedWork.title: Christ Healing the Man with Dropsy

rows.editorialReason: The anonymous monastic painting matches the episode in title, but object identity and style are weak; do not promote it to selected Calendar art.

recommendedWork.title: The Exaltation of the True Cross

rows.editorialReason: Ricci's Exaltation is an exact feast narrative and a strong period fit; original research points to an unresolved first-party image.

rows.observance: Seven Sorrows of the Blessed Virgin Mary
rows.editorialReason: The Seven Sorrows subject is already the editorial selection for the novena cover; its photo identity remains unverified. Propose a separate feast-date scope, not a new painting.
No verified painted encounter with the questioning Pharisees is documented in existing date leads. A generic Christ portrait would be contextual, not exact Gospel.
Await exact Ember-lesson and Gospel linkage before naming an event painting. Do not infer an image from the word Ember.
Await exact 1962 Friday Ember proper and its gospel. Preserve the date's liturgical specificity.
Multiple lessons and a distinctive Ember Mass make a generic feast image insufficient. Needs a date-specific scene cue.
The existing Lazarus resurrection paintings are a DIFFERENT miracle and cannot serve as exact Gospel imagery. Retain an explicit paralytic gap.
Andrei Mironov's image has a thematic title but is not an owner-approved historic Baroque painting. Prefer research for a period work.

Lotto's Madonna del Rosario is the protected, approved Rosary cover, but its protection is slot-specific. Calendar reuse would need distinct approval; existing Met Fifteen Mysteries remains an alternative.
Vignon's Baroque parable scene is a specific, strong match to the Sunday Gospel; retain gallery identity review, without treating a title as photo certification.

recommendedWork.title: Martyrdom of Saints Simon and Jude

rows.editorialReason: Lochner's two-saint martyrdom is an exact feast narrative but its Gothic treatment falls outside the preferred dark Baroque family. Keep as fallback only.

rows.observance: Dedication of the Archbasilica of Our Holy Savior
rows.editorialReason: Ricci's identified fresco depicts the specific dedication, but the image is rights-held. Keep artwork proposal, not a publication commitment.
The existing Unforgiving Servant painting is not this parable. Needs the appointed Mustard Seed/Leaven narrative or explicit contextual fallback.
Joos van Cleve's Last Judgment is apocalyptic context, not an exact depiction of the foretold desolation; use only as a thematic candidate.
Rubens's Andrew martyrdom is a strong Baroque subject, previously tagged acceptable but unfinished. Avoid Prado photographic reproductions.

rows.observance: Feria V after III Sunday of Advent

The existing Visitation work is a strong Advent Marian illustration pending exact Ember Gospel confirmation; earlier artwork-level acceptance is not this day's placement approval.
Multi-lesson Ember Saturday; no unambiguous direct image match should be assigned from an Annunciation keyword alone.

rows.observance: Feria IV after IV Sunday of Advent
